study: Finkelstein et al. 2010, Problem Based Economics (NCEE 2010-4002, REL West)
delivery_evidence: PD = 40-hour economics course held over five days in summer 2007 (in-person workshop led by expert teachers), with five scheduled phone conferences as ongoing support during the year; primary/dominant mode is the in-person 5-day institute (Intervention section; methods). Phone conferences are a minor remote support component.
test_alignment_evidence: Two co-primary outcomes: Test of Economic Literacy (TEL), a published standardized independent test (distal), AND a UCLA CRESST researcher-made open-ended performance-task composite (proximal, developer-made) (Table 4.1, p.53).
curriculum_evidence: Intervention = Buck Institute's Problem Based Economics curriculum + PD; 'teachers received the curriculum materials' and the 5-day PD introduces this new curriculum (Intervention section, p.viii; methods).
outcome_timing_evidence: Both outcomes measured at end of the spring 2008 semester, end of the one-semester economics course (Table 4.1, p.53; design).
